title: Ms. Elmore's birth, church, organs and moves to Alexandria
summary: Ms. Elmore gives her birth in 1902 at Glencoe, her church upbringing, church organs and bass, moving to Lake Charles, Alexandria and New Orleans in 1938, and John Thompson's band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: All right. Let's see. We're talking to Ms. Elmore here right now. So we want to get when you were born and where. Well, I was born in 1902 in St. Mary Parish in a place called Glencoe, Louisiana, out from Franklin. That's near Baldwin or on the other side? Yeah, right near Baldwin. I know Jack Wilman from there. Jack Wilman, yeah. He's from Baldwin. Were you brought up in a church? You must have been. Yes. Which church was that? Methodist, ME. But I'm African Methodist now. You were just ME in those days? Uh-huh. I see. Well, my family were ME in here. But after my mother died, we all moved to Lake Charles, Louisiana. My aunt raised this. And then, well, I went to church a while, but we have to go, have to go with someone else. So she was an AME. And I just went along with her. How old were you when your mother died? Fifteen. I was fourteen. Fourteen. Oh, did we get your exact birth date? Did we get what day of the month you were born? Nineteen october. The month and the date? Oh, no. October 19th. I see. Mm-hmm. Did you hear any music out there, bands or anything? Well, not that I remember. They didn't have any bands, but they did have Cardin and they had organ music at that time. In the church? Uh-huh. Yeah. Did they have any organs outside the church at all? Well, at one home, they were, in case they were plentiful. Mm-hmm. Once in a while you'd go to a home and find one. And they played, it seemed like, with a cypher, you had to turn them, you know? So, uh, we had one at my church there. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. I see. Did they have any other instruments that they played on in your church? No. Just the oil of it. I see. Yeah. Mm-hmm. Some of these churches have all kind of things. Oh, mercy. Nowadays, yes. Nowadays. But in them days, you see, they weren't so plentiful. But, uh, now you can find all kind. And later on, after I grew up, then they had pianists. And then they had, uh, in one church, which I used to visit, I wasn't a member of that, but my aunt was. She, uh, this was a Baptist church. And, like, Baptist church, they had an organ and a, I guess you'd call that a bass. There was great big music, uh, like a violin, but it sit on the floor and they play it. Oh, great big one, huh? Yeah. Mm-hmm. Would they hold it between their legs or would they stand there? No, they just stand there and play it. I see. Well, that's a bass, yeah. Yeah. When did you come to the city? New Orleans. Nineteen, uh, 1938. Nineteen thirty-eight. Nineteen thirty-eight. Uh-huh. So you come here in late years. Yeah. You lived in Lake Charles all the time after you moved from, uh, St. Mary's? Well, no. I, uh, left there and then I lived in Alexandria twelve years. Uh-huh. And after the twelve years I went back to Lake Charles. See, who had a band in Alexandria? John Thompson had a band up there, I believe. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Did you ever hear that band? Uh-huh. What kind of music did he play? Well, they played songs, they had music like, you know, blues, but I, I'm something like her. I never did take to that kind of music. Uh-huh. I never fancied very much. We were. Mostly in the church? Yeah. Would the churches sing different songs in all these different places or did they sing pretty much the same? Well, they mostly sang the same thing. Uh-huh. The same books they were used. So, only after the sheep music came out, well, then you could buy the different music. I thought of something I want to ask her. Let me go back to her. Uh-huh. Did you ever sing what they call Dr. Watts hymns? Yeah. Yeah.
